questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Cambodia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Culture” part of the Cambodia article.

questions.proof: Cambodians are famous for a type of 'kah-tieu' called 'kah-tieu Phnom Penh' which has shrimp, beef balls, fried garlic, pork broth and chicken.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Cambodia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Cambodia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Cambodia article.

questions.proof: It is near Vietnam, Laos, and Thailand.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Cambodia?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Cambodia article.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Cambodia has border issues with _____ and Thailand over lost territories.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “issues”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Cambodia article, under the heading “Foreign relations”.

questions.proof: Cambodia has border issues with Vietnam and Thailand over lost territories.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Cambodia attended its first Olympic Games in _____ and participated in two more before warfare and civil strife interrupted its attendance.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Cambodia article, under the heading “Sports”.

questions.proof: Cambodia attended its first Olympic Games in 1956 and participated in two more before warfare and civil strife interrupted its attendance.
